title: Tôi rửa tay ở đây được không?
englishTitle: Can I wash my hands here?
pronunciation: toy zoo-ah tai uh day dook khong
summary: Different ways to say "Can I wash my hands here?" in Vietnam, with the phrase to start with, reusable pieces, and related next steps.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Use this when you only need a sink or hand-washing spot. Useful in markets, food areas, and roadside stops. Learn the full phrase first; the related phrases below help when the exchange moves one step further.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: This pattern turns the phrase into a yes-or-no question. Keep the main need together so the question stays natural.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Tôi rửa tay ở đây được không? is the version to learn first for "Can I wash my hands here?". Use this when you only need a sink or hand-washing spot. If the person hesitates, show the place, object, or screen that gives the phrase context.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use this when you only need a sink or hand-washing spot. Use it in bathrooms, soap, paper, water, and basic personal needs when one clear sentence will work better than a long explanation.

sections.title: Watch out
sections.body: Some places may not have paper or soap available. Asking early avoids an awkward surprise.

sections.title: Local tip
sections.body: Ask directly and follow gestures. People may simply point you toward the right place.

sections.body: Use these next when the conversation moves one step forward.
